overview: A single Java 17 service implements URL creation, redirect lookup and asynchronous click analytics. H2 provides durable relational persistence. Redirects use a cache-aside map for hot mappings and invoke a ClickRecorder contract without waiting for analytics persistence. The API contract is represented by lightweight HTTP handlers because the reference project intentionally contains no web framework.

components.name: ShortenerService
components.responsibility: Validate URLs and aliases, allocate IDs, generate base62 short codes, persist mappings and resolve redirects.
components.contract: create(longUrl, alias) returns a ShortUrl; resolve(code) returns the stored mapping or empty.

components.name: JdbcShortUrlRepository
components.responsibility: Persist URL mappings in H2 using JDBC and enforce unique short codes and aliases.
components.contract: create, findByCode and existsByAlias operations backed by a relational table.

components.name: Cache
components.responsibility: Keep frequently accessed URL mappings in memory to reduce database reads on redirects.
components.contract: get, put and invalidate by short code.

components.name: ClickRecorder
components.responsibility: Accept successful redirect events without coupling redirect latency to analytics persistence.
components.contract: record(ClickEvent) must return immediately and must not propagate analytics failures to the redirect path.

components.name: AsyncClickRecorder
components.responsibility: Implement ClickRecorder with a bounded queue and background JDBC writes.
components.contract: Successful redirect events are queued; full queues drop events and increment a drop counter.

components.name: AnalyticsService
components.responsibility: Query total clicks, daily click counts and the latest click time for a link.
components.contract: stats(code) returns aggregated analytics from persisted click events.

components.name: ShortenerHttpServer
components.responsibility: Expose REST-like HTTP endpoints using the JDK HttpServer API.
components.contract: POST /api/links creates links, GET /{code} redirects, and GET /api/links/{code}/stats returns analytics.

openApiYaml:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: URL Shortener API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /api/links:
    post:
      summary: Create a short link
      requestBody:
        required: true
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Created
        '400':
          description: Invalid URL or alias
        '409':
          description: Alias conflict
  /{code}:
    get:
      summary: Redirect to the original URL
      responses:
        '302':
          description: Redirect
        '404':
          description: Unknown code
  /api/links/{code}/stats:
    get:
      summary: Get click analytics
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Analytics
        '404':
          description: Unknown code

decisions.rationale: The reference project provides H2 and no application framework, so JDBC keeps the generated system dependency-free.
decisions.tradeoffs: A production deployment would normally use a managed relational database with connection pooling and operational backups.

decisions.rationale: The workload is explicitly read-heavy and cached mappings can avoid database reads.
decisions.tradeoffs: An in-memory cache is local to one process and requires invalidation if deletion is added later.

decisions.rationale: Redirect latency must not depend on analytics persistence.
decisions.tradeoffs: Events can be dropped when the bounded queue is full, so analytics is explicitly best effort.

decisions.decision: Generate seven-character base62 codes from database IDs
decisions.rationale: A database-generated unique numeric ID provides a deterministic source for collision-free generated codes.
decisions.tradeoffs: Sequential IDs make the code space enumerable; production deployments may need an opaque identifier strategy.

scalabilityNotes: The expected read-heavy workload is handled by a local cache for hot redirects.
A single H2-backed process is suitable for the reference implementation but is not a production 99.999% multi-region architecture.
Analytics writes are decoupled from redirects through a bounded asynchronous queue.
The architecture can evolve to a distributed cache and replicated relational store without changing the ClickRecorder contract.
